result: The study recruited 120 Polish adolescents and young adults (60 with dyslexia, 60 controls) matched for sex, age, and socioeconomic status, examining both EEG and MRS biomarkers of E/I balance. The dyslexic group showed expected deficits in reading and reading-related tasks, validating the group assignment. This represents the first direct test of the neural noise hypothesis using combined EEG power spectrum measures and 7T MRS measurements of Glu and GABA.

result: No evidence was found for group differences in aperiodic EEG components (exponent and offset) between dyslexic and control groups, either at rest or during a language task. These findings contradict a previous study by Turri et al. (2023) that reported decreased exponent and offset in dyslexic participants.
